mainTopic: How a קמיע becomes proven (writer versus amulet), and whether amulets have קדושה that would forbid bringing them into a בית הכסא.
overview: This עמוד opens at the end of a ברייתא: even a proven amulet may not be fastened to a bracelet or ring on שבת, because of מראית העין. The גמרא then notes a contradiction about how an amulet becomes proven. It answers that one source proves the writer is an expert, and the other proves the amulet itself works. רב פפא lays out which cases prove the writer, which prove the amulet, and which prove both. He also asks about three amulets that healed one person, and that question ends in תיקו. Next the גמרא asks whether amulets have קדושה. After ruling out saving them from a fire and גניזה, it finds the real practical question: may one enter a בית הכסא with an amulet? It tries to prove from our משנה that amulets are not holy, and pushes the proof away several times. In the end, a healing amulet may even be held in the hand, so the proof fails, and the discussion continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Do not attach the amulet to a bracelet or ring
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its rule. Even a proven amulet may not be wrapped onto a bracelet or ring and worn into the רשות הרבים, because of מראית העין.
steps.simpleTranslation: …to a bracelet or a ring and go out with it into the public domain, because of how it looks.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא that already said a person may go out on שבת with a proven amulet. It adds one limit: he may not attach it to a bracelet or ring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing a proven amulet counts as treating a medical need, so it is allowed. But if it is fastened to jewelry, onlookers will think he is wearing jewelry that is not allowed, rather than something worn for healing. That is the problem of מראית העין.

keyTerms.meaning: A bracelet or bangle
A ring
The public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden
How something looks to others; avoiding actions that appear to be forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: This עמוד begins in the middle of a sentence. The words 'and he should not wrap it' come from the end of the previous דף. The amulet itself is allowed; only the way it is worn is the problem.

phrases.english: to a bracelet or a ring
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence from the previous דף: 'provided he does not wrap it…'

phrases.english: and go out with it into the public domain.
Because of the appearance (of wrongdoing).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from the previous דף that defined a proven amulet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A proven amulet may be worn on שבת, but not fastened to a bracelet or ring, because of מראית העין.

steps.title: Another source requires healing three different people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines a proven amulet as one that healed three people. This seems to contradict the earlier definition, which was one person healed three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: Which is a proven amulet? Any one that healed three people alike!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier definition by quoting a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source counted three healings of the same person. This ברייתא demands three different people. So which test makes an amulet 'proven'?

keyTerms.meaning: An amulet, a written charm worn for healing
Proven, expert, tested as effective
Alike, equally; here meaning three separate people

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
Which is a proven amulet?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁרִיפֵּא שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם כְּאֶחָד!
phrases.english: Any one that healed three people alike!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition of קמיע מומחה found in the same source as step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition that a proven amulet is one that healed one person three times.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A contradicting ברייתא requires three different people, so the two definitions clash.

steps.title: Proving the writer versus proving the amulet
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. Three different people healed proves the writer is an expert. One person healed three times proves that specific amulet works.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about proving the man an expert; that one is about proving the amulet effective.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each source is testing something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Healing three different people shows the writer's skill is reliable, not just a fluke with one patient. Healing the same person three times shows that this particular written amulet works. Both sources are correct, each for its own purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult'; introduces a resolution
'This… that'; assigns each source to a different case
To prove or establish as expert
The man, meaning the writer of the amulet

steps.whyThisMatters: This creates two separate kinds of 'proven': a proven writer and a proven amulet. רב פפא builds on this next.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is for proving the man (the writer) an expert,
that one is for proving the amulet effective.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source addresses a different subject (writer versus amulet).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to define the same thing, a proven amulet, in conflicting ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three people healed proves the writer; one person healed three times proves the amulet.

steps.title: רב פפא's three cases
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא lays out three cases. In the first, both the writer and the amulets are proven. In the second, only the writer is proven. In the third, only the amulet is proven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is obvious to me: three amulets for three people, each three times, proves the man and proves the amulet. Three amulets for three people, each one time, proves the man but not the amulet. One amulet for three people proves the amulet but not the man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא applies the distinction from step 3 to concrete cases. He shows exactly which results prove the writer and which prove the amulet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three different amulets each working three times shows the writer's skill and also shows each amulet works, so both are proven. Three amulets each working once on three people shows skill across patients, but no single amulet was tested three times, so only the writer is proven. One amulet healing three people proves that amulet, but the writer only succeeded with one piece of writing, so he is not proven.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is obvious to me'; a clear ruling
Three
Times (occurrences)
Became proven or established as expert
One

steps.whatToRemember: Proving the writer requires success across different amulets and people. Proving an amulet requires that specific amulet to work three times. Three amulets × three people × three times proves both.
steps.confusionAlert: In the last case, one amulet healed three people, yet the writer is not proven. The success came from a single written amulet, not from his skill shown across several different amulets.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is obvious to me
three amulets for three people,
each one three times —
the man is proven an expert and the amulet is proven effective.
Three amulets for three people,
each one a single time —
the man is proven, the amulet is not proven.
One amulet for three people —
the amulet is proven, the man is not proven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the writer/amulet distinction from step 3 and applies it to specific scenarios.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three amulets × three people × three times proves both the writer and the amulets. Three amulets × three people × once proves only the writer. One amulet × three people proves only the amulet.

steps.title: Three amulets for one person: is the writer proven?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about a case where one writer made three different amulets for one person, and each one healed him. The amulet is surely not proven, but is the writer proven?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If three amulets were made for one man, what is the law? The amulet is certainly not proven. But is the writer proven or not? Do we say each amulet healed him, so the writer is an expert? Or maybe it was this man's own luck that responded to the writing?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks about a mixed case that does not fit the categories from step 4. One person was healed three times, but each time by a different amulet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each amulet worked only once, so no single amulet is proven. The writer seemed to succeed three times, but always on the same person. Maybe the writer is skilled, or maybe this one patient's מזל made him respond to amulets in general.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; he raised a question he could not resolve
Was proven to be an expert or proven to work
Healed
Fortune or luck; a person's personal destiny
Or perhaps; introduces the second side of a question

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
Three amulets for one man, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Three different amulets, each healing the same person once.

phrases.english: The amulet is certainly not proven.
phrases.notes: Each amulet worked only one time.

phrases.english: Is the man (the writer) proven, or not proven?
Do we say: look, it healed him,
or perhaps it is the fortune of this man (the patient)
that is receptive to the writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a case that falls between the categories רב פפא laid out in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does one person healed by three different amulets prove that the writer is an expert?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer is given. The question ends in תיקו.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רב פפא's question unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to רב פפא's question, so the question remains open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source settles the matter. Both possibilities, a skilled writer or the patient's luck, remain open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 5 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no ruling on whether a writer is proven when one person is healed by three different amulets.

steps.title: Do amulets have holiness?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is raised: do amulets carry קדושה, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Do amulets have holiness, or perhaps they do not have holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks whether amulets are holy objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Amulets often contain names of ה' or פסוקים, so they might be treated like holy writings. Or, since they are made for healing, they might not have קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the חכמים)
Holiness; the status of a sacred object
Amulets

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Do amulets have holiness,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא אֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם קְדוּשָּׁה?
phrases.english: or perhaps they do not have holiness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about amulets, unrelated to proving an expert.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether amulets have the status of holy objects.

steps.title: What practical law depends on this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which practical law the question about holiness would affect.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. Before answering, the גמרא wants to know what practical difference the question makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question about status only matters if some law depends on it. The next steps will try several possible laws until they find one that is truly unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What is the practical difference?

phrases.english: For what law (does this matter)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical case the question in step 7 is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law the question of an amulet's holiness affects.

steps.title: It cannot be about saving amulets from a fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the question is about saving amulets from a fire on שבת. It rejects this because a ברייתא already says they are not saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the question is about saving them from a fire, come and hear: Blessings and amulets, even though they contain letters of holy names and many matters from the תורה, are not saved from a fire. They burn where they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one practical case: may you save amulets from a fire on שבת? It quickly shows that this law is already known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holy writings may be saved from a fire on שבת. But a ברייתא clearly says amulets are left to burn, even though they contain holy names. Since the answer is already known, this cannot be the case behind the question.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggestion that will be rejected
To save them (from a fire)
A fire
They burn in their place; they are left to burn

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא does not prove that amulets have no קדושה. It only shows that the fire law is already settled, so the question must be about some other law.

phrases.english: If you say: to save them from a fire,
come and hear:
The blessings and the amulets,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן אוֹתִיּוֹת
phrases.english: even though they contain letters (of holy names)
and many matters from the Torah,
we do not save them from a fire,
and they burn in their place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 8 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out saving amulets from a fire as the case behind the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא already says amulets are not saved from a fire, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: It cannot be about burying amulets
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the question is about גניזה, burying holy writings. It rejects this because even a name of ה' written on a bed leg must be cut off and buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is about burial. Come and hear: If a name of ה' was written on the handles of vessels or on the legs of a bed, one must cut it off and bury it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second practical case: must a worn-out amulet be buried? This law is also already known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a name of ה' written on a bed leg must be buried, then an amulet with holy names surely must be buried too. So גניזה also cannot be the case behind the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new suggestion after the last one failed
Respectful burial of holy writings
The legs of a bed
He must cut it off

phrases.english: Rather, regarding burial.
Come and hear:
If (a name of ה׳) was written on the handles of vessels
or on the legs of a bed,
he must cut it off and bury it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 failed, offers a second answer to step 8 and rejects it too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out גניזה as the case behind the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא already requires burying a name of ה' wherever it is written, so amulets surely need גניזה.

steps.title: The real question: bringing amulets into a bathroom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on the true practical case: may a person enter a bathroom while wearing an amulet?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is about entering a bathroom with them. What is the law? Do they have holiness, so it is forbidden? Or perhaps they have no holiness, so it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally finds the practical law that depends on the question: entering a bathroom with an amulet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holy writings may not be brought into a bathroom. If amulets have קדושה, a person would have to take them off first. If they do not, he may keep wearing them inside.

keyTerms.meaning: A bathroom or outhouse
It is forbidden
It is permitted

phrases.english: Rather, (the question is about) entering a bathroom with them.
What is the law?
Do they have holiness, so it is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא אֵין בָּהֶן קְדוּשָּׁה — וּשְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: or perhaps they have no holiness, so it is permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two failed suggestions, gives the real answer to step 8's question about which law is at stake.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical law depends on whether amulets have קדושה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether one may enter a bathroom while wearing an amulet.
steps.whyThisMatters: This now frames the original question as a real, unresolved law that a source can test.

steps.title: A proof begins from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a proof from our משנה. Since one may not go out with an amulet from a non-expert, it follows that one may go out with an amulet from an expert.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Nor with an amulet when it is not from an expert.' This implies that if it is from an expert, he may go out with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings our משנה to try to answer the bathroom question. It begins by drawing an inference: a proven amulet may be worn outside on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids going out with a non-expert's amulet, so an expert's amulet must be allowed. This inference sets up the proof. The next step completes the argument by showing how this connects to the bathroom.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert; here, a proven writer or amulet
This implies; introduces an inference from a source
He may go out (wearing it)

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בְּקָמֵיעַ בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִן הַמּוּמְחֶה:
phrases.english: 'Nor with an amulet when it is not from an expert.'
This implies: if it is from an expert, he may go out (with it).

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע וְלֹא בְּקָמֵיעַ בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִן הַמּוּמְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins trying to answer the bathroom question defined in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether amulets have קדושה, as it applies to entering a bathroom.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, which implies that one may go out on שבת with an amulet from an expert.

steps.title: Finishing the proof: a holy amulet would lead to carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: If amulets were holy, he would remove one before the bathroom and come to carry it four אמות in רשות הרבים. Since the משנה still permits going out with it, amulets must not be holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that amulets have holiness, then sometimes he will need to go to the bathroom. He will have to take the amulet off, and he may come to carry it four אמות in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the proof it started in Step 12. It shows that a holy amulet would cause a שבת problem, so the משנה's permission suggests amulets are not holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A holy amulet cannot come into a bathroom, so the wearer must take it off. Then he holds it in his hand, or forgets it is off, and ends up carrying it four אמות in רשות הרבים. חז"ל did not worry about this and permitted an expert's amulet, so it seems amulets have no קדושה and may be brought into a bathroom.

keyTerms.meaning: Amulets worn for healing or protection
Holiness
Sometimes
Bathroom
Four cubits in the public domain, the amount of carrying that breaks שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not about wearing the amulet. Wearing it is permitted as a form of clothing or jewelry. The worry is about the moment he takes it off and holds it in his hand, which counts as carrying.

phrases.english: And if you say that amulets
have an element of holiness,
sometimes he will need to go to the bathroom,
phrases.notes: He would have to remove the amulet first.

phrases.english: and he will come to carry them
four cubits in the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ קְמֵיעִין יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם קְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 12
steps.raayaObject: That amulets have no קדושה, so one may enter a bathroom wearing one
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, which permits going out with an amulet from an expert

steps.title: The משנה may be talking about a root amulet
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away: the משנה may mean an amulet made of herbal roots, which has no writing and no holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? An amulet made of roots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. It says the משנה may be talking only about an amulet made of roots, not one with writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A root amulet has no name of ה' in it, so it has no קדושה at all. It can go into a bathroom, and the carrying problem never comes up. So the משנה tells us nothing about written amulets.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? Used to narrow a source to a specific case
Roots or herbs used for healing

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With an amulet of roots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 13 by narrowing the משנה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה, not the question itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may refer only to root amulets, which have no holiness anyway

steps.title: A ברייתא treats written and root amulets the same
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the law applies equally to a written amulet and a root amulet, so the משנה cannot be limited to root amulets.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: the law is the same for a written amulet and for a root amulet!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 14. A ברייתא says written and root amulets follow the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the law of going out with an expert's amulet applies to written amulets too, the carrying problem is back. So the root-amulet answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: A written amulet

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: both a written amulet
and an amulet of roots!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֶחָד קָמֵיעַ שֶׁל כְּתָב וְאֶחָד קָמֵיעַ שֶׁל עִיקָּרִין
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה speaks only of root amulets
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly includes written amulets in the same law

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is about a dangerously ill person
steps.stepSummary: A new attempt: the משנה may be about a חולה שיש בו סכנה, who may bring even a holy amulet into the bathroom because of danger to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with here? A sick person whose life is in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second way to block the proof. The משנה may be about someone whose life is in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a person in danger, even a holy amulet may stay on in the bathroom because saving life comes first. Then he never takes it off and never carries it. This does not prove that amulets are not holy for everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A sick person whose life is in danger
Rather. Introduces a new answer after the previous one failed

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
With a sick person who is in danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed answer of Step 14 with a new limitation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה proves amulets have no קדושה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה may be about a life-threatening case, where even a holy amulet may be kept on

steps.title: The ברייתא includes the non-dangerously ill too
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא says the law applies equally to a sick person in danger and one not in danger, so the second answer also fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: the law is the same for a sick person in danger and a sick person not in danger!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 16 with the same ברייתא. It says the law covers both kinds of sick people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a person who is not in danger may also go out with the amulet, the carrying problem returns for him. So the danger answer cannot explain the משנה either.

keyTerms.meaning: A sick person whose life is not in danger

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֶחָד חוֹלֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ סַכָּנָה
phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: both a sick person in danger
and a sick person not in danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֶחָד חוֹלֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ סַכָּנָה וְאֶחָד חוֹלֶה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ סַכָּנָה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה speaks only of a dangerously ill person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly includes a sick person who is not in danger

steps.title: Since the amulet heals, holding it in the hand is also fine
steps.stepSummary: The final rejection of the proof: since the amulet heals, carrying it in the hand is also permitted, so there is no carrying problem and the משנה proves nothing about קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the amulet heals, even if he holds it in his hand, that is also fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the proof in a new way. It removes the carrying problem altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amulet is permitted because it heals, and it heals in the hand just as it does around the neck. So if he takes it off for the bathroom and holds it, he does nothing wrong. The משנה could permit amulets even if they are holy, so this proof falls. The bathroom question is not yet decided, and the גמרא continues on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it heals
Even though
He holds it in his hand
It is fine, it is permitted

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה fails. A healing amulet may even be held in the hand on שבת, so the משנה's permission does not show whether amulets are holy. On this עמוד, the question of bringing an amulet into a בית הכסא is still not decided. The גמרא continues the discussion on the next עמוד.
steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say amulets are holy, and it does not say they are not. It only says the משנה cannot be used to decide the question.

phrases.english: Rather, since it heals,

phrases.english: even though he holds it in his hand,
it is (also) fine.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה does not prove that amulets lack קדושה, so the bathroom question is not settled by this proof. The discussion continues on the next עמוד.
